published_statement: As the tree states it (no external source states it in these words): throatmass.py:98-99 'Closed only by a general existence theorem for the static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat class, which nobody has.  NOT DONE HERE.'; throatmass.py:174-176 O5_ANSWERED_BY '... Closed only by an existence theorem for the static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat class'. Closest READ external statements: Sanders 2007.14311v2 p.2: 'It appears, however, that the static solutions of the semi-classical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system have not been studied before (except the Minkowski vacuum). One reason may be that the system under consideration does not have any interesting classical static solutions.' and sec. 7: 'a more detailed investigation will be necessary to settle this question for general states in an Einstein static universe, or even in general static spacetimes.' HPS gr-qc/9701064 p.2: 'no one up to now has succeeded in writing down a bona-fide wormhole solution of either the classical or semiclassical Einstein field equations'; p.3: 'The results of the present calculation may be taken as numerical evidence for the existence of Lorentzian wormholes'; p.8: 'The redshift function however, does not approach a constant value as l -> infinity, so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat.' 2604.01047 (2026) sec. 1.5: 'In the case of cosmological spacetimes, the full nonlinear analysis has been carried out in [78]' -- its survey names no existence theorem for the static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat class.
published_hypotheses: H1 (tree) the class: static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat metrics solving G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab> with a quantum field source -- the tree does not say whether <T_ab> is an exact renormalised expectation value in a Hadamard state (Sanders / Juarez-Aubry sense) or the Anderson-Hiscock-Samuel analytic approximation (HPS sense, the one throatmass.py's families and hpscentre.py use)
H2 (tree) 'general existence theorem' -- scope not stated: existence of at least one member, of a non-trivial (non-flat) member, or of a member for given data / mass
H3 (tree) 'which nobody has' -- a universal negative over the literature, asserted with status word 'none (NOT DONE HERE)', no search record attached
H4 (tree) 'closed ONLY by' -- that O5 (does an AF self-consistent static solution with m < 0 exist?) can be settled by nothing but such a theorem

Sanders (READ): rigorous class = full semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system, free scalar, state and metric solved together; static solutions 'not studied before (except the Minkowski vacuum)' as of 2020/2021
HPS (READ): AHS approximate <T_ab>, xi = 1/6, m = 0, temperature 0, throat data eq. (9); numerical, 'local solutions'; not asymptotically flat (f unbounded)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED QUALIFIER 'non-trivial', throatmass.py:98-99 and :174-176: the static spherically symmetric AF class is NOT empty -- flat space with the Minkowski vacuum is a member (Sanders p.2 excepts it by name) and f = const, r = l solves HPS eqs (5)-(7) identically (computed, rederive C1). So 'an existence theorem for the class' is already trivially true; what is absent is existence of a NON-FLAT member (or of a member for prescribed data). The tree's wording omits this.

OVERSTATED 'only', throatmass.py:98 ('Closed only by') and :175-176: on a finite model (z3, rederive C3) an exhibited AF self-consistent solution with m < 0 decides O5 = yes with no theorem, a no-go decides O5 = no, and a general existence theorem E is consistent with BOTH answers, so E alone closes nothing. A logical discrepancy in the tree's framing, not an error of the literature. Already superseded in the tree: hpscentre.py:303-308 O5_ANSWERED_BY lists 'an asymptotically flat self-consistent solution with m < 0' and FO/FFKP evaluations as answers, with 'the nonlinear regular-centre existence theorem' as one route among several; ledger.py SUPERSEDED_WORDING keeps the DOCKET 62 wording.

UNSPECIFIED SOURCE TERM, throatmass.py:94-99: the paragraph is about HPS's printed system (AHS approximation), but 'semiclassical solution' in the existence-theorem literature (Sanders, Juarez-Aubry, Pinamonti-Siemssen) means the exact renormalised <T_ab> of a Hadamard (or symmetric) state. The two are different classes; hpscentre.DOMAIN_WORD (hpscentre.py:299-302) records that the AHS approximation is established only for asymptotically flat spacetimes. The tree's claim is plausibly true in both readings, but it is two claims.

UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE WITHOUT A SEARCH RECORD, throatmass.py:99 'which nobody has': stated as fact; the tree's own discipline for the neighbouring zero (throatmass.py:40-58, 'NOT-FOUND, not NO', with a control that the search can return solutions) is not applied to this sentence. The honest word is NOT-FOUND.

C1: flat space f = 1 (and f = c > 0), r = l solves HPS eqs (5)-(7) (transcribed from the READ page text) with all three residuals exactly 0; Misner-Sharp mass 0; control f = 1, r = l + 1/l does NOT solve eq. (5) (residual 0.13079 at l = 2) -- the class is non-empty, so only NON-TRIVIAL existence is at issue. C2: HPS's printed asymptotics give F -> infinity (not AF), m = 0 at leading order on R = l. C3 (z3, 4-element model with vacuity guard): exhibited AF m < 0 solution => O5 decided yes; no-go => O5 decided no; existence theorem E is satisfiable with O5 and with not-O5 -- the 'only' fails as logic. lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite in its empirical form: whether an existence theorem exists is a mathematical and bibliographic question; no measured quantity enters it, and no later measurement can create or remove a theorem. What the 1997-2021 literature lacked was TECHNIQUE, not data: HPS had only the AHS approximate <T_ab> and numerics (and HPS's own solution is not AF); Sanders (2021) had rigorous tools only for compact ultrastatic slices, naming the non-compact case 'more challenging, because the symmetry group becomes non-compact'. Evidence that the gap is closing, not closed: Juarez-Aubry 2022 (static constrained IVP) and 2024/2026 (well-posedness without symmetry for a special state class) -- both NAMED-NOT-READ. Evidence for the tree's side: every READ source through April 2026 names no such theorem. Having the later papers might change the conclusion (by exhibiting a non-flat AF static member for a special state class) or might not; that cannot be decided here.
grade_evidence: The claim is a universal negative over the literature and cannot be established or refuted here. For it: Sanders 2021 (READ) says static semiclassical solutions had not been studied except the Minkowski vacuum; HPS 1997 (READ) gives numerical evidence only and says its own solution is not asymptotically flat (rederive C2); the 2026 survey 2604.01047 (READ) names no such theorem. Against, or undetermined: the mandated discover_papers sweep did not run (alphaXiv quota), and two later Juarez-Aubry papers on static spacetimes and on well-posedness without symmetry (2011.05947, 2412.08402) are NAMED-NOT-READ. Separately, and independent of the literature question, two framing discrepancies are COMPUTED: (a) the class is non-empty (flat space solves HPS eqs (5)-(7) identically, C1), so the missing theorem is one for NON-TRIVIAL existence -- a qualifier the tree omits; (b) 'closed ONLY by an existence theorem' fails as logic (z3, C3): an exhibited AF m < 0 solution or a no-go would each close O5, and an existence theorem alone closes neither -- already superseded in hpscentre.py:303-308. These are discrepancies in the tree's wording, not refutations of the literature claim, so they do not make the grade WRONG; they mean that even if confirmed the grade would be NARROWED, not STANDS.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED (the expected ceiling): reading 2412.08402 and 2011.05947 at source and finding no non-flat static spherically symmetric AF solution or theorem there, plus a completed discover_papers sweep with no contrary hit -- the literature claim would then stand as NOT-FOUND, narrowed by the two computed wording discrepancies ('non-trivial' qualifier; 'only'). To WRONG for the literature half: a READ paper proving existence of non-flat static spherically symmetric AF solutions of the semiclassical Einstein equations with exact renormalised <T_ab> (e.g. a stealth state on a non-flat vacuum background, if 2412.08402's class contains one). STANDS is not reachable while the tree's wording keeps 'only' and omits 'non-trivial'.
